Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

sir noun

in polite address

also madam, ma’am, yes, sir, excuse me, sir

classical

Sen. Ep. 3.1 (Lewis & Short: “in respectful greeting, like our Sir”)
Mart. 6.88 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 379: to a superior

domine

vocative of dominus, used in address

By Seneca’s day one greeted a man whose name escaped one as dominus (Sen. Ep. 3.1, cited by Morgan–Owens s.v. Mr.); earlier it is what a slave called his master. To a woman, domina.

Other words

  • domina — madam

    vocative of domina, used in address · also used · classical · M-O s.v. Mrs.: ma’am; Traupman 343

  • bone vir — sir, my good man

    also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 5.2.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 379; Traupman 68

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Friendly or ironic, mostly in comedy (Lewis & Short s.v. bonus); Traupman gives it for “sir!” to an equal.

Examples

  • Cupiō, domine, sī id pāce liceat tuā.

    I should like to, sir, if you will allow it.Erasm. Coll., Monitōria paedagōgica, I 36

  • age tū, illūc prōcēde, bone vir!

    come on, you, step forward, my good man!Plaut. Capt. 5.2.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also master, gentleman, lady.
